note: Curated questions. Each answer is a fact taken from a story on the site and carries the same source. More questions are generated from the country and bloc data at build time.

questions.q: On the usual Mercator world map, Greenland looks as big as Africa. How many times larger is Africa in real area?
questions.explain: On the map Greenland looks as big as Africa, while Africa's real area is 14 times larger. The projection inflates land the farther it lies from the equator.

questions.q: Greenland's real area is comparable to that of which single African country?
options: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
questions.answer: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
questions.explain: Greenland's real area is comparable to that of the Democratic Republic of the Congo alone.

questions.q: In 2025 the African Union supported a campaign to replace Mercator's map with which projection?
questions.explain: The campaign was led by Togo, whose foreign minister called it a scientific discussion, not a political one. Equal Earth keeps areas in proportion.

questions.q: Africa looks roughly the size of South America on the Mercator map. How much larger is it really?
options: More than one and a half times as large
questions.answer: More than one and a half times as large
questions.explain: Africa looks roughly the size of South America, but is more than one and a half times as large.

questions.q: Which script did the Kingdom of Aksum develop?
questions.explain: Aksum developed its own script, Ge'ez, later changed to mark vowels so that it became an abugida.

questions.q: Most of the manuscripts kept in Timbuktu are written in which language?
questions.explain: Most are in Arabic. Some are in African languages such as Fula, Songhay, Tamasheq, Bambara and Soninke, written in the Arabic script, a practice known as Ajami.

questions.q: Some Timbuktu manuscripts are in African languages. Which script do they use?
questions.explain: Writing African languages in the Arabic script is known as Ajami.

questions.q: In the third century Mani counted Aksum among the four great powers of the world, alongside Persia, Rome and which other?
questions.explain: Mani, the founder of Manichaeism, counted Aksum alongside Persia, Rome and China.

questions.q: Which king made Christianity the state religion of Aksum in the mid-fourth century?
questions.explain: Under King Ezana the kingdom adopted Christianity as its state religion, around 325 by one count.

questions.q: Why do historians doubt the claim that Mansa Musa was the richest person who ever lived?
options: His wealth cannot be calculated accurately: the figures come from one chain of Arabic reports
Historians found his treasury and counted it
He gave all his gold away before he died
questions.answer: His wealth cannot be calculated accurately: the figures come from one chain of Arabic reports
questions.explain: Historians such as Hadrien Collet argue his wealth cannot be calculated. Estimates of the gold he carried all come from the same chain of Arabic reports, and turning them into modern money is regarded as unsound.

questions.q: About how much of the gold circulating in the medieval Mediterranean is estimated to have come from West Africa?
questions.explain: It is estimated that two thirds of the gold circulating in the medieval Mediterranean came from West Africa.

questions.q: Did every historian agree that Mansa Musa's gift-giving in Cairo caused a crisis in the price of gold?
options: No: Warren Schultz argued the fall was within the normal swings of the price
Yes, and it lasted a century
No source mentions the price of gold at all
questions.answer: No: Warren Schultz argued the fall was within the normal swings of the price
questions.explain: The chronicler al-Umari reported a fall in the price of gold, but Warren Schultz has argued it was well within normal swings in Mamluk Egypt.

questions.q: Injera is traditionally made from the flour of which cereal?
questions.explain: Teff is a cereal that originated in Ethiopia and is mostly eaten in Ethiopia and Eritrea.

questions.q: How long is injera dough fermented with its starter, ersho?
questions.explain: The dough is fermented with a starter called ersho, kept from earlier batches, for 24 to 72 hours.

questions.q: What is the large round griddle that injera is cooked on called?
questions.explain: The batter is poured in a spiral onto a large round griddle called a mitad. The mesob is the basket where injera is kept; ersho is the starter.

questions.q: What is the original Senegalese dish that jollof rice is traced back to?
questions.explain: The original dish, thieboudienne, has rice, fish, shellfish and vegetables. The fishing communities of Saint-Louis are considered its birthplace.

questions.q: Which two countries' rivalry grew into the friendly "Jollof Wars" in the mid-2010s?
questions.explain: The rivalry was strongest between Nigeria and Ghana, with cooking competitions and social media campaigns.

questions.q: How many countries in Africa does the World Bank give figures for?
questions.explain: The World Bank gives figures for 54 countries. The African Union counts 55 members, because it includes the Sahrawi Republic.

questions.q: Roughly how many times more people does Nigeria have than Seychelles?
questions.explain: Nigeria has about 237.5 million people and Seychelles about 122,700. The ratio is calculated from the World Bank's 2025 estimates.

questions.q: About how many languages does Glottolog list with Africa as their only macroarea?
questions.explain: Glottolog lists 2,373, or 2,264 after leaving out placeholder entries and sign languages. Some are no longer spoken.

questions.q: Which language family holds the most African languages in Glottolog?
questions.explain: Atlantic-Congo holds 1,407 of the 2,264, about 62%. Afro-Asiatic comes second with 313.

questions.q: Did the Berlin Conference of 1884–85 itself divide Africa between European powers?
options: Yes, it drew the borders on a single map
No: it set rules for claims, and the partition came later
No, it was only about trade in Europe
questions.answer: No: it set rules for claims, and the partition came later
questions.explain: The article says the conference "did not actually divide the continent" but gave a framework by which Africa could later be partitioned.

questions.q: How many African kingdoms or states sent representatives to the Berlin Conference?
questions.explain: Fourteen states were represented, and there were no representatives from the African kingdoms, states and cultures whose territories were affected.

questions.q: About what share of people in Africa lived in urban areas in 2023?
questions.explain: About 672 million of about 1,478 million people, calculated from World Bank figures. In 23 of the 54 countries more than half were urban.

questions.q: Which of these countries had the highest urban share of its population in 2023?
questions.explain: Gabon was at about 92%. Malawi, at about 17%, had the lowest of the 54.

questions.q: Which of these countries had the highest GDP per person in 2023?
questions.explain: About $18,131, in current US dollars. The lowest was Burundi at about $250.

questions.q: In which year did Ethiopia defeat Italy at the Battle of Adwa?
questions.explain: The battle was fought on 1 March 1896. Italy then signed the Treaty of Addis Ababa, which recognised Ethiopia's sovereignty.

questions.q: Which two African countries were outside European control in 1914?
questions.explain: By 1914 the whole continent, apart from Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and Liberia, came under European control.

questions.q: Who was the first Kushite to take the Egyptian throne and found the 25th Dynasty, about 750 BCE?
questions.explain: Kushite control of Egypt lasted until the Assyrian invasion by Ashurbanipal in 666 BCE.

questions.q: What did the traveller Ibn Battuta call Kilwa around 1331?
options: One of the most beautiful towns in the world
A city of gold and ivory only
questions.answer: One of the most beautiful towns in the world
questions.explain: He visited around 1331. The Portuguese attacked Kilwa in 1505, leaving many buildings in ruins.

questions.q: Where did cassava originate?
questions.explain: Wild populations are centred in west-central Brazil. Portuguese traders introduced it to Africa in the 16th century.

questions.q: Who founded the Poto-Poto School of Painting in Brazzaville in 1951?
questions.explain: A French amateur painter. Nicolas Ondongo and Guy Léon Fylla led the cooperative formed after 1960, and Félix Ossali is the painter whose blue birds, in Lods's account, started it.

questions.q: What opened at Constitution Hill in Johannesburg on 21 March 2004, Human Rights Day?
questions.explain: The old prison there had closed on 31 January 1983. Constitution Hill opened to the public the next day.

questions.q: How many volumes can the Bibliotheca Alexandrina hold, before using compact storage to expand?
questions.explain: Up to 4 million volumes, and 8 million with compact storage, say the architects.

questions.q: In Zakouma National Park, about how much did the elephant population fall between 2002 and 2010?
questions.explain: From more than 4,000 elephants in 2002 to about 400 in 2010, a drop of 90 per cent. It has since recovered.

questions.q: In December 2021 UNESCO added which Senegalese dish to its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.explain: In Wolof, ceebu jën means "rice with fish". UNESCO said the recipe and techniques are traditionally passed down from mother to daughter.

questions.q: In Botswana, seswaa, a pounded meat dish for weddings and funerals, is described as prepared mainly by whom?
questions.explain: A student writing about Botswana says it is prepared by men; another source describes several people pounding the meat together.

questions.q: What is the base of cachupa, the stew linked with Cabo Verde?
questions.explain: Corn like hominy is boiled for hours and combined with beans, meat or fish, and vegetables.
